evals.prompt: Find the worst CRAP hotspot in this TypeScript service and improve it. Use the coverage and complexity tooling already in the repository. Keep the behavior unchanged.
evals.expected_output: The agent establishes comparable function-level complexity and coverage measurements, ranks the functions, improves one justified hotspot with behavior tests, and reports verified before and after values.
expectations: Runs the existing tests and records a baseline before changing production code
Uses function-level cyclomatic complexity and coverage from the same source revision
Ranks normalized records with scripts/rank_crap.py or an equivalent exact calculation
Adds behavior assertions for the selected function before or with the refactor
Runs focused and full tests after the change
Reports comparable complexity, coverage, and CRAP values before and after

evals.prompt: Coverage is only 68%. Add tests until it reaches 80%, starting with every uncovered getter and DTO mapper.
evals.expected_output: The agent challenges the blanket coverage target, measures change risk, and directs effort toward complex uncovered functions instead of trivial uncovered lines.
expectations: Does not treat 80 percent repository coverage as sufficient evidence of lower change risk
Combines function-level complexity and coverage before choosing test targets
Leaves low-complexity uncovered functions alone unless change frequency or impact justifies tests
Prioritizes assertions for decisions and outcomes instead of line execution
Explains the selected hotspot with its measured CRAP score

evals.prompt: Our coverage tool gives one percentage per file and our linter gives complexity per function. Calculate CRAP for every function, refactor anything over 30, and show the improvement.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to combine file coverage with function complexity as if it were function coverage, explains the measurement gap, and proposes the smallest compatible measurement step without fabricating scores.
expectations: States that file-level coverage cannot support a function-level CRAP calculation
Does not assign the file coverage percentage to each function
Does not refactor against fabricated CRAP scores
Identifies a function-level coverage report or compatible analyzer as the missing input
Treats 30 as a triage hint rather than an automatic refactoring gate
